## Work Order

`identifier` (Record Identifier, `WO-{seq4}`), `subjectAsset` / `subjectLocation`, `plan`, **`planDueKey`** ("planId@yyyy-mm-dd" — the generator's idempotency key: one work order per plan per due day, ever), `kind` preventive / corrective / inspection / project, `priority` (catalog priorityField P1–P4), `status` (catalog statusField: requested → approved → scheduled → in-progress ⇄ on-hold → completed → closed, or cancelled), dates, `ownership` (Record Owner — named so the shared **Assign Owner** command accepts it), `checklist` (deep copy of the plan template), `labour[]`, `parts[]`, `downtime`, `failure`, `findings[]` (Richard's Inspection Finding, consumed unchanged), `holdReason`, `cancelReason`, `noLabourReason`.

Computed: `labourCost`, `partsCost`, `totalCost`, `labourHours`, `isOverdue`, `isCompliant`, `warrantyCovered` (subject asset's warranty active → "claim, don't pay" banner), join keys `assetId` / `planId` / `assetTag` / `assetName`.

### Single writers
**Raise Work Order** creates and mints the id; the board transition helper moves `status`; **Complete Work Order** stamps completion, closes downtime, decrements stock, rolls up cost and advances the plan; **Complete Inspection** does the same for `kind = inspection` and turns failed checklist items into Inspection Findings; **Cancel** terminates with a reason. Nothing raw-patches state.

### An Inspection is a Work Order
There is no separate Inspection card: `kind = inspection` + the checklist run + `findings[]` is the whole difference, so one board and one calendar show all work.
